## Limitations and Future Work

While KIVI is highly effective, the authors note a few areas for improvement: [...] 1. Memory Capacity: Servers run out of VRAM, limiting how many users can be served concurrently.
2. Memory Bandwidth: The GPU spends more time moving this massive cache from main memory to its internal processors than it does actually performing calculations.

While quantizing model weights is common, quantizing the KV cache to ultra-low precision (like 2-bit) usually destroys model accuracy.

## The KIVI Method [...] When serving LLMs, the "KV cache" is a major headache. To avoid re-calculating attention for every new word, models store the "Keys" and "Values" of previous tokens in memory. As batch sizes grow and context windows lengthen (e.g., a chatbot remembering a whole book), this cache balloons in size.

results.title: KIVI: A Tuning-Free Asymmetric 2bit Quantization for KV Cache | alphaXiv
results.content: Large Language Models (LLMs) face significant memory challenges during inference, particularly from the Key-Value (KV) cache that stores intermediate attention states. This cache prevents redundant computation during auto-regressive text generation but can consume terabytes of memory for large batch sizes and long contexts, often exceeding the model parameters themselves. The KV cache creates a bottleneck that limits inference throughput and increases serving costs. [...] This paper is cited as a key related work that also tackles the KV cache bottleneck. KIVI's authors reference FlexGen's use of 4-bit group-wise quantization for both key and value caches, positioning their own asymmetric quantization strategy as a more nuanced and effective approach for lower bit-rates. [...] KIVI (Key-Value Cache Quantization with Streaming Support) addresses this challenge through a systematic approach that first analyzes the distribution characteristics of KV cache elements, then designs a specialized 2-bit quantization algorithm based on these insights. Unlike previous approaches that apply uniform quantization strategies, KIVI recognizes that keys and values have fundamentally different distribution patterns that require asymmetric treatment.
